## The Bakersfield Brief — August 14, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. We start the day with a high of 95° and air quality at a moderate 54 AQI. Overnight, a troubling welfare check involving a woman seen crying for help in a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace dominated the scanner traffic. Read on for the full overnight report, today’s forecast, and the top local stories — including Bakersfield Christian High School’s push to rebound from a state title loss and Kern County’s role in shaping a national addiction recovery toolkit. We’ve also got your community good note and a look at what’s coming up this week.

## The Kern Overnight

A night that opened with a road-rage pair stalling traffic on White Lane and closed with a stolen van on Kentucky Street and a fender dispute between big rigs at the Flying J. Law enforcement carried most of the load: a 90-plus mph DUI south of the Grapevine, a reported theft from a mobile home park on Barlow Road, and the night's most serious call — an attempt-to-locate after a woman was seen crying for help out the window of a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace. Fire crews were comparatively quiet: a residential alarm that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion and rescue unit before the air went quiet.

Around 11:34 p.m., Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver's window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound. It's the kind of call dispatchers don't sit on: no description of plates or direction of travel beyond southbound, so the broadcast went out citywide for any unit to catch the truck. No further update was heard on the air before the feed moved on.

Just after 9:23 p.m., city units were sent to White Lane for a possible road-rage disturbance: a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both eastbound, repeatedly stopping and blocking the roadway. Dispatched as a 415 vehicle with no further update heard.

At 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street. Officers took the report; no arrests were announced on the air.

About 11:39 p.m., CHP broadcast a 23152 on southbound I-5 south of the Grapevine — a newer black pickup at speeds over 90, passing on the shoulder, the driver seen drinking from an open container. Units were responding as the feed moved on.

Shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park: the victim's burgundy Freightliner was hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 95° and a low around 67° tonight. It's currently 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 54 — moderate.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield Christian High School is looking to rebound from a state title loss, with the Eagles working to right the wrongs of the past. The team is determined to learn from its recent defeat and come back stronger in the upcoming season, focusing on improvement and resilience.

**According to 23ABC,** Bakersfield police and fire chiefs shared their Fourth of July findings at a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Despite a 6% drop in fire-related responses compared to 2025, officials say more work remains to deter illegal fireworks use.

**23ABC tells us that** Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, helped shape a national addiction toolkit aimed at addressing treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among professionals who worked with federal agencies to develop best practices for recovery programs.

**KGET 17 said that** Kern County officials will inform the public on local ICE activity during a community forum on August 25. The event will provide residents with information and a platform to discuss concerns regarding immigration enforcement in the area.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a slice of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This support will enhance local aviation infrastructure and services, benefiting the community.

## Coming up this week

Here’s what’s on tap for the week ahead:

On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m.

Wednesday, August 19, features the Water Board meeting at 10:00 a.m.

Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission convenes at 5:30 p.m.

And on the calendar for today, August 14, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1:00 p.m., the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee gathers at 12:00 p.m., and the Special Laws and Legislation Committee convenes at 12:00 p.m.

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater hosts PEPPER with CYDEWAYS tonight, August 14. Later this month, catch Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.
